finding.description: The object held by the man in the foreground is a white stick, but its reflection in the mirror appears as a blue razor.
The blue razor in the mirror reflection morphs into a black comb as the man brings it to his hair, and then morphs back into a razor when he returns it to his face.

The motion of the hand brushing against the face and hair is created by rapidly looping the same few frames forward and backward (a 'boomerang' effect). This violates the forward flow of time and creates unnatural repeated beats.

A rapid, continuous scratching/clicking sound effect plays throughout the video, but the frequency and timing of the sound do not match the visual strokes of the object against the man's face or hair. There is no visible cause for the continuous sound.
The man's right arm instantly teleports from his cheek to the top of his head without continuous movement, and his fingers snap from a curled grip to a flat pose in a single frame.
The man's right arm instantly teleports from the top of his head back down to his cheek, and his hand snaps from a flat pose back to a curled grip in a single frame.
As the man raises his hand from his face to his hair, the small clear comb in his hand spontaneously transforms into a larger black comb. There is no visible action to explain swapping the object.
As the man lowers his hand from his hair back to his face, the large black comb spontaneously transforms back into the small clear comb. No swap or object exchange is visible.

The spatial trajectory of the foreground man's hand moves backwards over his head, while the reflection's hand moves downwards across the forehead. The reflection's geometric movement is completely uncoupled from the physical object it reflects.
